PAN flower-like superstructures synthesis
nodes.procedure: 50 mL of AN and 50 mg of AIBN were combined with 50 mL of ACE solvent to prepare PAN flower-like polymer superstructures. The reaction was conducted at 70°C for 2 h in a tightly sealed glass vial to ensure an oxygen-free environment, utilizing an oil bath and nitrogen (N2) gas protection, without stirring, which is critical for the polymerization process. The resulting white product was dried overnight at room temperature in a vacuum oven to remove any unreacted monomer and solvent, which exhibited a distinct flower-like morphology.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of the PAN flower-like superstructures. 50 mL of AN and 50 mg of AlBN were combined with 50 mL of ACE solvent...

nodes.name: CNF synthesis (stabilization + carbonization)
nodes.procedure: The as-prepared PAN flower-like superstructures were subjected to a thermal stabilization process in the air to enhance their structural integrity prior to carbonization. Specifically, the samples were heated to 230°C in an air atmosphere for 2 h, with a slow ramping rate of 0.2°C/min. Following the stabilization process, the stabilized PAN particles were subsequently carbonized at 900°C in an N2 atmosphere to prepare CNF.

nodes.name: S-doping of CNF
nodes.procedure: S atoms were introduced into CNF matrix by adopting 2,2'-bithienyl as the sulfur source. Specifically, 50 mg of 2,2'-bithienyl was first dissolved in 10 mL of methanol. Subsequently, 150 mg of CNF matrix was dispersed into the solution and the mixture was vigorously stirred for 1 h to ensure homogeneous impregnation. The resulting suspension was then transferred to an oven and dried at 60°C to remove the solvent completely. Finally, the dried composite was subjected to pyrolysis under an inert atmosphere at 800°C for 1 h, yielding the S-doped CNF matrix through thermal decomposition and carbonization processes.

nodes.name: Os-NP@NC synthesis
nodes.procedure: 10 mL of OsCl3 (1 mg/mL) solution was slowly added into 150 mg CNF powder to prepare the precursor. After stirring for 2 h, the solution was then placed in an oven to dry at 60°C. Subsequently, the dried black powders were pyrolyzed in a furnace at 950°C to synthesize the N-doped carbon supported Os nanocrystals sample (Os-NP@NC).

nodes.name: Os-NP@NC
aliases: Os nanocrystals supported on N-doped carbon matrix

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images of Os-SA@SNC and Os-NP@NC exhibit well-preserved three-dimensional porous flower-like architectures inherited from CNF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the SEM images of the as-prepared Os-SA@SNC (Fig. 1B and SI Appendix, Fig. S9) and Os-NP@NC (SI Appendix, Fig. S6) exhibit well-preserved three-dimensional porous flower-like architectures that were inherited from CNF.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM shows Os nanocrystals uniformly dispersed in Os-NP@NC with average size of 3.01 nm; lattice fringes of 0.237 nm and 0.216 nm corresponding to (100) and (002) planes of hcp Os.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1C and SI Appendix, Fig. S7, Os nanocrystals were uniformly dispersed in the Os-NP@NC sample. Corresponding size-distribution histograms derived from 150 nanocrystals indicate an average Os size of 3.01 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: AC HAADF-STEM depicts atomically dispersed Os sites uniformly anchored on S,N-doped CNF support in Os-SA@SNC with no large nanoparticles; confirms Os nanocrystals in Os-NP@NC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1D clearly depicts that atomically dispersed Os sites were uniformly anchored on the S, N-doped CNF support, with no large nanoparticles observed in the Os-SA@SNC sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping demonstrates homogeneous distribution of C, N, O, Os in Os-NP@NC and C, N, S, O, Os in Os-SA@SNC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The homogeneous distribution of C, N, O, and Os elements in Os-NP@NC was further clearly demonstrated by the corresponding energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping (SI Appendix, Fig. S8).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES determines Os mass loading in Os-NP@NC as 2.01 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It has been determined that the mass loading of Os in Os-NP@NC is about 2.01 wt% according to the inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry result (SI Appendix, Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: N2 adsorption-desorption isotherms show type I behavior for both catalysts; BET surface areas are 211.69 m²/g for Os-SA@SNC and 208.52 m²/g for Os-NP@NC with micropores, mesopores, and macropores.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the Brunauer-Emmett-Teller model, the specific surface areas of Os-SA@SNC and Os-NP@NC are 211.69 and 208.52 m² g⁻¹, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of Os-NP@NC shows diffraction patterns consistent with hcp Os plus amorphous carbon peak; Os-SA@SNC shows only CNF pattern with no Os nanoparticle peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD result of Os-NP@NC (Fig. 1F) reveals the expected diffraction patterns. ... Regarding Os-SA@SNC, the XRD pattern is almost the same as that of pure CNF, revealing no corresponding diffraction peak for Os nanoparticles or clusters.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman ID/IG ratios are 0.978 for Os-NP@NC and 0.991 for Os-SA@SNC, lower than CNF (1.08), indicating reduced defect levels.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the Raman results of the Os-NP@NC and the Os-SA@SNC (SI Appendix, Fig. S15), the calculated intensity ratios of ID/IG are 0.978 and 0.991, respectively, lower than that of CNF.

nodes.characterization_summary: Os 4f XPS shows peaks at 50.54 eV (4f7/2) and 53.28 eV (4f5/2) for Os-NP@NC and 51.54 eV (4f7/2) and 53.25 eV (4f5/2) for Os-SA@SNC, shifted to higher binding energy indicating higher oxidation state; S 2p in Os-SA@SNC shows peaks at 161.37 eV (metal-S), 165.68 eV (C-S-C), 166.51 eV (S-O).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Os 4f XPS spectra (Fig. 2A), the peaks representing Os 4f7/2 and Os 4f5/2 for Os-NP@NC can be observed at 50.54 and 53.28 eV, respectively... the binding energies of Os in Os-SA@SNC exhibited a shift toward higher values in comparison to the Os-NP@NC, measuring at 51.54 and 53.25 eV. Fig. 2B exhibits the S 2p spectra of Os-SA@SNC. The S 2p curve of Os-SA@SNC displayed three peaks at 161.37 eV (metal-S bond), 165.68 eV (C-S-C), and 166.51 eV (S-O).

nodes.characterization_summary: Os L-edge XANES shows absorption edge shift to higher energy and stronger white line for Os-SA@SNC > Os-NP@NC > Os foil, confirming higher oxidation states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2C, the absorption edge for Os in Os-SA@SNC is more positive, as compared with Os-NP@NC and Os foil, signifying a higher oxidation state.

nodes.characterization_summary: Os L-edge EXAFS shows prominent Os-Os peak at 2.35 Å in Os-NP@NC (shorter than bulk Os foil ~2.50 Å); Os-SA@SNC lacks Os-Os peak, shows single Os-heteroatom peak at 1.46 Å; curve-fitting reveals Os-N3S1 coordination with Os-N at 2.01 Å (CN=3) and Os-S at 2.18 Å (CN=1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the Os L-edge EXAFS analysis, a prominent peak at 2.35 Å is observed in the Os-NP@NC sample (Fig. 2D), which is associated with the Os-Os scattering pathway... for the Os L-edge EXAFS spectra of the Os-SA@SNC sample, the absence of the Os-Os peak indicates that Os exists in an atomically dispersed state... The first shell coordination numbers for Os-N and Os-S are 3 and 1, at the distances of 2.01 Å and 2.18 Å, respectively.
